title: 返世幽魂 Revenant
body:
**从死亡中归来的韧性灵魂，执行命运的工作。**

**平均身高：**165cm-188cm/5'5"-6'2"
**平均体重：**45kg-91kg/100-200 lb

**属性调整：**+2敏捷；+2体质或魅力
**体型：**中型
**速度：**6格
**视觉：**昏暗视觉

**语言：**通用语，另外任选一种
**技能奖励：**+2坚韧，+2威吓
**不死特性：**在考虑有关不死关键字的效果时，你被视为不死生物。你同时被视为活体生物。
**往世生命：**选择一个除返世幽魂之外的种族。在考虑是否满足前提时，例如专长或典范之道的前提，你同时被视为那个种族的成员。
**超凡活力：**当你的生命值降到0或更低且受濒死状态影响时，你可以选择陷入晕眩，而不是失去意识。你如常地进行死亡豁免，且如果你失败一次，则你失去意识而不是晕眩。
**黑暗收割：**你具有⟦黑暗收割 Dark Reaping⟧威能。

⟦黑暗收割 Dark Reaping⟧

死亡通常代表着通往来世的大门，或自然生命的终结。然而，有时死亡仅仅是开始。对于某些被选中的个体，鸦后或其他掌管死亡的力量会阻隔他们前往下一阶段，将灵魂引回凡界。在这些情情况中，命运对他们另有安排。

返世幽魂并非作为一具无目标的尸体而苏醒，而是作为一个被赋予新使命的失落灵魂的具现化。这样的生物行走于两个世界之间。当返世幽魂在生者之间穿行时，它也存在于阴影之中，被那些它已不再拥有的生活的模糊记忆所萦绕。

返世幽魂不像其他种族那样建立定居点或共享共同的文化。连接这些活死人的唯一纽带，是一系列共同的物理特征以及相似的起源与命运。所有的返世幽魂都是在其死后被有意送回凡界的。虽然已死，却又无法通往死亡黑暗之门后的彼岸，这曾经活着的灵魂被重新构成为一个返世幽魂。

死亡与命运之神常在凡界需要代理人，而他们的从神与化身并不总能应付所有需要完成的事务。因此，返世幽魂被召唤而生。然而，影响众神及其如何介入凡界的规则，在凡人眼中往往神秘莫测，甚至自相矛盾。正因如此，返世幽魂似乎是在没有明确指引甚至没有完整生前记忆的情况下重返世间。

返世幽魂通常以成年形态出现，身体已完全发育成熟，本能地能够应对周围的世界。大多数在墓地或墓穴等死者之地苏醒，对往事仅有模糊的记忆，且通常怀有一种强烈的驱动力，要去完成某个依稀记得的任务或某个定义模糊的使命。

大多数返世幽魂只记得生前生活的一些片段，以及回归世间之前那一片安宁黑暗。有些人需要时间来处理这些破碎的记忆与强烈的驱动力；另一些人则更为从容地接受了自己的新存在，而没有过多的分析与内省。许多人会忆起一个女性的声音——柔和而悠扬，仿佛黑羽之翼轻柔的扇动——那个声音伴随着他们走出阴影回到凡界的苏醒之中。那话语温柔却坚定，常常是返世幽魂归来时一切冲动的源头。尽管每个返世幽魂重返世间的方式各不相同，但大多数人都记得那些与黑暗一同飘来的话语：“起来吧，我的勇士，”那声音命令道，“还有事情要做。”

---
**外貌特征 Physical Qualities**

返世幽魂是由鸦后或其他来世之力重现生者模样的死者之魂。返世幽魂不会以不死怪物的形态出现，甚至不会与生前的自己有任何相似。当鸦后使灵魂重生时，它们作为她特殊的造物而存在，拥有她所选择与创造的身躯。如此，这些灵魂便始终被标记为鸦后力量的代表。它们自死亡的阴影中现身，已是完整而成熟的形态，准备去处理那些它们被送回世间来处理之事。

返世幽魂的身形相对其身高而言偏瘦，但其躯体拥有一种与其外观不符的奇异坚韧。返世幽魂的肤色与人类相似，但皮肤灰白，面容凹陷。最常见的是全黑的眼睛，其中闪烁着一点赤红光芒，但其他怪异的眼睛颜色——包括黄色、白色、银色与金色——也并非罕见。在某些情况下，眼睛会散发出幽灵般的光芒。返世幽魂的发色通常在黑色至灰色、白色的范围内。返世幽魂能长出面部毛发，男性常蓄有胡须或小胡子，使其灰白的面容更为突出。

返世幽魂的面容与皮肤，显然将其与其他类人种族区别开来。返世幽魂的面孔带有一种面具般的特质，可能令凡人不安。在返世幽魂四肢末端附近的皮肤上，会出现粗糙的暗色鳞片，标记着其为鸦后允许重返生者世界之人。返世幽魂的手脚生有坚硬黑色的指甲与趾甲，形似利爪。

**态度和信仰 Attitudes and Beliefs**

每个返世幽魂以不同的态度面对重回世间这件事。有些人乐在其中，渴望找回他们已失去并遗忘的生活。另一些人则以炽热的激情拥抱新的存在，借此掩埋那些仍萦绕他们的过往碎片，并努力在凡界中活下去。

有些返世幽魂无法忍受那些一闪而过的、已不再属于他们的过去残影，他们渴望找到一条路回到那被驱逐出的黑暗。这些返世幽魂很清楚最快回归那片阴影的舒适之路，便是尽可能迅速而高效地完成那些置于他们面前的任务。他们并非寻求终结其存在，而是渴望重返坟墓的安宁——那是他们第一次穿越生命时挣得的安宁。

许多返世幽魂可能显得疏离而冷漠，但他们能够体验与其他种族相同的全部情感。他们只是需要时间来调和所面对的种种矛盾——从陌生而崭新的躯体，到破碎的记忆，以及一个强大存在所指示的半懂不懂的任务，而那存在或许愿意，也或许并不愿意向他们解释正在发生的一切。

**返世幽魂团体 Revenant Communities**

返世幽魂不会形成社群，也不构建社会。然而，他们确实会与他人建立联系——通常是与其他能够帮助他们实现目标的冒险者之间。有些人甚至会定居于其他种族的社群中，通常是因为那地方唤起了他们依稀记得的某些事物，又或是因其靠近他们需完成之任务的相关所在。例如，那个社群可能靠近一道通往堕影冥界的传送门，或正处在鸦后之敌活跃的区域之中。

每个返世幽魂都是独特的，但与堕影冥界的联系使大多数返世幽魂偏好深色与有助于不引人注目的服装。无论是出于黑色幽默，还是作为对他人的警告，他们的衣物与装备上常带有死亡或职责的象征符号。返世幽魂使用乌鸦羽毛、骨头、锁链、墓碑与颅骨作为装饰。

**角色扮演返世幽魂 Roleplaying a Revenant**

在创建返世幽魂角色时，可考虑以下几点。

**你和其他凡人不同。** 返世幽魂不像凡人种族那样生活与繁衍。事实上，他们根本不是真正的种族。每一个返世幽魂，都是因鸦后（或其他死亡之力）的意志而现身于世间。她——或与她达成协议的某人——在每一个被送回凡界的灵魂心中，都已埋下了特定的目的。

**你怀有目的。** 这个目的对返世幽魂而言，可能是清晰明确的，也可能是一个必须在安息之前解开的谜。返世幽魂或会执着地追求这一目标，或会反抗那命运，试图避开既定的宿命。这一目的甚至可能变化——当走向终局的脚步迈出一步，更大的目标便会显现。这很大程度上取决于是谁将返世幽魂带回世间。

若那灵魂的归来是鸦后之命，那么该返世幽魂或许会在鸦后所预见的未来中扮演重要角色。鸦后或许会派遣一位灵魂，将某个逃脱了死亡之人或物引向它应有的终结；而那返世幽魂之所以被选中，或许正因它与目标之间存在过往的联系。

**你的记忆是支离破碎的。** 返世幽魂通常只记得生前的一些片段——恰好足以将他们推向将他们唤醒之目的。许多人甚至不记得自己的名字，因此会取一个贴合自身性情的新名。记忆在梦境与灵光一闪中浮现，往往由返世幽魂自身的经历所触发。在市场上偶然擦肩，可能会想起那个人曾是一生挚友；瞥见一只苍白的手拂过光亮的发丝，可能会让返世幽魂的心中忆起一段失落的爱。每一段记忆都有其目的：奖励、惩罚、诱饵，或援助。它们都是真实的，但将返世幽魂唤醒的那股力量，有时也能控制他们忆起哪些真实记忆。

**你似曾相识，却无人知晓。** 返世幽魂的稀少使得鲜少有人对其有所了解。宗教学者或曾与返世幽魂有过接触的人或许知道得更多，但对大多数人而言，返世幽魂是陌生且异质的存在——只会在深夜低矮的篝火旁低语的流言中被提及。

**返世幽魂特征：**机敏，冷漠，坚定，恐怖，顽强，高尚，务实，悲剧一般的

**男性姓名：**Bane, Carver, Dredge, Erak, Riven, Rook, Scourge, Sever, Snipe, Wrath

**女性姓名：**Blessed, Charm, Fable, Ire, Lash, Nihil, Raven, Sunder, Vengeance

title: 歌利亚斯 Goliath
body:
**群山中的部落游牧者，如岩石般强壮，山峰般骄傲。**

**平均身高：**218cm-234cm/7'2"-7'8"
**平均体重：**127kg-154kg/280–340 lb

**属性调整：**+2力量；+2体质或感知
**体型：**中型
**速度：**6格
**视觉：**普通视觉

**语言：**通用语，矮人语或巨人语
**技能奖励：**+2运动，+2自然
**山之坚韧：**你在意志上获得+1种族加值。
**蛮力运动：**当你进行运动检定来跳跃或攀爬时，掷骰两次且使用任一结果。
**石之忍耐：**你具有⟦石之忍耐 Stone's Endurance⟧威能

⟦石之忍耐 Stone's Endurance⟧

歌利亚斯是栖居在山间的游牧种族，他们将生命看作一场宏大的竞赛。他们分散的族群从来没有在低地世界的政治中扮演过重要角色，但自从荒神首次塑造出群山和山谷之时，他们便游荡于山脉之间。歌利亚斯高大强壮，他们崇敬自然的原力并借此增强自己的力量。

扮演歌利亚斯，如果你希望…

• 比几乎任何其他人都坚韧强壮。
• 掌控崎岖不平的山坡。
• 成为偏好野蛮人、战士和守望者的种族成员。

---
**外貌特征 Physical Qualities**

站立起来身高大约在7到8英尺的歌利亚斯甚至比龙裔更高大。他们的皮肤是灰色或棕色的，上面带有深色的斑纹，他们相信这些斑纹暗示着每个歌利亚斯命运或天数的某些方面。他们的手臂，肩膀，躯干和头部分布着由硬币大小、宛如鹅卵石的骨质增生。他们闪亮的蓝色或绿色眼睛上方有着骨质的棱脊。男性歌利亚斯是秃顶，女性有深色的头发，她们通常把头发留长并扎成辫子。

歌利亚斯有着与人类相似的寿命。

**角色扮演歌利亚斯 Roleplaying a Goliath**

歌利亚斯被他们对于竞争强烈的热爱所驱动。任何能够被当作挑战的东西都会使歌利亚斯开始记分，追踪他们的战友和自己的进展。一位歌利亚斯战士也许会谈论在某特定地城中首先让敌人挂彩的次数他比团队中的游荡者多了多少，并且他肯定在自己脑中将这次表现与他上一次冒险相比较。在歌利亚斯中他们的竞争表现为良性的较劲。作为一个种族，他们无法容忍作弊者、炫耀者和输不起的人，但当歌利亚斯无法达到自己过去的成就时他们会对自己非常严苛。

近乎莽撞的胆量也是歌利亚斯的常见特征。他们从不畏惧高处，可以轻松爬上陡峭的山崖，跃过宽阔的裂口。狩猎和采集的游牧生活方式，使他们对在下一道山脊或峡谷尽头的东西怀有强烈的好奇心。对游荡的猎手来说，这种好奇心能让他们找到更好的猎场，或是一处原本可能无从发现的优质水源。

歌利亚斯尊敬并敬畏自然世界，而歌利亚斯的探险者也通常汲取原力。在歌利亚斯中德鲁伊和萨满比起牧师更常见，歌利亚斯的祭司——被称作观天者(skywatcher)——呼唤自然精魂与祖先的次数，远远多于向众星之海中遥远神祇的祈祷。一些歌利亚斯部落也崇敬寇徳，梅洛拉和艾梵德拉，特别是那些与其他种族频繁接触的部落。那些经常与矮人交易的部落也会向摩拉丁献祭。

**歌利亚斯特征：**好竞争，勇敢，发奋图强的，好奇的，强有力的，可靠的，焦躁不安的，可信任的

**男性姓名：**Aukan, Eglath, Gauthak, Ilikan, Kavaki, Keothi, Lo-Kag, Maveith, Meavoi, Thotham, Vimak

**女性姓名：**Gae-Al, Kuori, Manneo, Nalla, Orilo, Paavu, Pethani, Thalai, Uthal, Vaunea

title: 工匠侏儒 Tinker Gnome
body:
**平均身高：**81cm-99cm/2'8"–3'3"
**平均体重：**20kg-25kg/44-55 lb

**属性调整：**+2智力；+2体质或敏捷
**体型：**小型
**速度：**5格
**视觉：**昏暗视觉

**语言：**通用语，另外任选一种
**技能奖励：**+2神秘，+2贼活
**快速修理：**你能以一个次要动作，进行神秘检定来禁用、辨识或感知魔法现象，以及进行贼活检定来开锁、辨识或关停装置，而不是标准动作。不过如果你这么做，则因为比较匆忙，你在此检定上受到-4减值。
**随手可用：**你获得除徒手攻击以外的临时武器的擅长。
**实验修正：**你具有⟦实验修正 Lab Conditioning⟧威能。

⟦实验修正 Lab Conditioning⟧

No one is precisely sure where tinker gnomes originated, since most of their earliest records were destroyed in a fire resulting from dubious experiments in advanced record-keeping technology. Despite this event, most tinker gnomes insist that they can trace the personages and events surrounding their family lines all the way back to their creation by the god Reorx. This assertion suggests that entire swaths of tinker gnome history are the product of sheer invention. To anyone who knows tinker gnomes, such a hypothesis seems a strong possibility.

Tinker gnomes are industrious to the extreme, exhibiting an obsessive need to build and redesign devices to help with every facet of their hectic lives. These gnomes challenge the limits of their world's scientific and magical knowledge on a daily basis. The average tinker gnome generally regards those few members of the race who are uninterested in technology as either lazy or insane, since satisfaction with the status quo and reliance on mundane solutions is nearly unheard of in tinker gnome society.

Though all tinker gnomes have a penchant for invention and engineering, relatively few are truly gifted in this area. The bulk of gnomish experimentation relies on trial and error, and most gnomes cheerfully acknowledge that the majority of their efforts end in failure. This fact does not disturb them, however; they are always ready to move onward to their next pet project.

---
**外貌特征 Physical Qualities**

Tinker gnomes average about three feet in height, and around fifty pounds in weight—slightly stout, but still nimble. Their hair is fine and pale—usually platinum blond or white—and most of the males grow luxuriant beards and mustaches. Tinker gnomes' skin comes in varying shades of tan, and wrinkles develop at an early age.

When on the job or traveling, tinker gnomes prefer to wear heavily modified thick leather aprons festooned with all manner of small tools. A tinker gnome is always prepared to make improvements, no matter the situation.

**态度和信仰 Attitudes and Beliefs**

The need for innovation among tinker gnomes is legendary. Tinker gnomes think nothing of spending years—even decades—in the creation of complex (and often faulty) gadgets with no practical purpose. The creators of such devices seem to have little or no concern about safety in testing their dubious creations, and the results of such tests are sometimes fatal. Rare is the dedicated tinker gnome who lives to a ripe old age.

The majority of other races find tinker gnomes difficult to understand. Tinker gnomes speak quickly and endlessly, stringing together long sentences without care for natural pauses in the conversation or social cues. They feel that they have to race to complete their trains of thought before they are lost forever. More often than not, tinker gnomes end their sentences only after the listener verbally or forcibly instructs them to stop.

Tinker gnomes foster a love of bureaucracy that transcends even the most dedicated middlemen of other races and societies. Dozens—if not hundreds—of guilds, many of which feature overlapping areas of expertise, drive the tinker gnome settlements. If a tinker gnome cannot find a suitable guild for his or her branch of investigation, the gnome does not hesitate to found a new one—regardless of interest, need, or purpose.

Every tinker gnome has three names. The first name is the given name, which details the name and deeds of every member of the gnome's family tree. The second name is a shortened version, which merely points out the highlights of the family history. The third name is a nickname, usually bestowed upon the gnome by members of other races. The nickname usually consists of the first few syllables of the gnome's full name. Most gnomes find these nicknames to be a mild indignity, but those who have regular dealings with other races tolerate their use.

The patron deity of the tinker gnomes is Reorx, the Creator. But the tinker gnomes are not especially religious, so they pay their deity little more than lip service, except for the observance of the Lifequest (see below). Tinker gnome priests do exist, but they are few and far between.

**工匠侏儒团体 Tinker Gnome Communities**

More than ninety-five percent of all tinker gnomes on Krynn dwell in a single dormant volcano. The gnomish name for the volcano is nearly a hundred words long, and most other races cannot pronounce it at all. Therefore, it has earned the sobriquet Mount Nevermind. The Naming Guild insists that this nickname was the utterance of an early human visitor to the settlement, who shouted "Never mind!" after a friendly member of the Greeting Guild attempted to welcome the beleaguered man to the mountain.

Tinker gnomes occasionally visit or even dwell in human cities, though most humans who live near them take great pains to limit their need for redesigning items, since such well-meaning endeavors can result in the malfunction or even destruction of useful devices. Some tinker gnomes also make their homes in predominantly kender and dwarven communities, though the gnomes tend to isolate themselves within their own enclaves.

**角色扮演工匠侏儒 Roleplaying a Tinker Gnome**

Here are a few points to consider when creating a tinker gnome character.

**There is always a better way.** Every task, no matter how mundane or minute, can be improved through study, industry, and creativity. Why use a mousetrap when you can design and build a Wind-Powered Troublesome Rodent Detection and Humane Extermination Automaton? True, the beta test version incinerated your cousin's foot, but that's a small price to pay for a rodent-free laboratory, and he seems to like his new Footmatic Pulley-Driven Prosthetic just fine (when it works, anyway).

**Never forget your Lifequest.** An important concept in tinker gnome society is the observance of the Lifequest. Every tinker has a Lifequest from birth, in addition to his or her normal duties and projects. Completion of the Lifequest safeguards the gnome and his or her bloodline, and it guarantees the gnome a place in the Afterlife. Lifequests are typically completed through the perfect development and understanding of a particular device. Few tinker gnomes have ever fulfilled a Lifequest.

**Invention exists for the sake of invention.** The prevailing sentiment within tinker gnome society is that creating a perfectly functioning device runs counter to the underlying principles of progress and advancement. A device that fulfills its task without complication or need for improvement is a creative dead end—anathema for most tinker gnomes. Those whose devices work regularly are often subjected to ridicule—or even exile in extreme cases.

**工匠侏儒特征：**Abrasive, cheerful, curious, disorganized, excitable, inventive, tenacious

**男性姓名：**Dagii, Drazen, Galtai, Haruuc, Oaan, Rhaano

**女性姓名：**Aerodyn, Cog, Conundrum, Dyffed, Gnimsh, Gnosh, Miggins, Saliman, Spanner

---
**工匠侏儒辅助威能**

title: 狗头人 Kobold
body:
**Reptilian tunnel dwellers who stick together to survive**

**平均身高：**107cm-122cm/3'6"-4'0"
**平均体重：**27kg-34kg/60–75 lb

**属性调整：**+2体质；+2敏捷或魅力
**体型：**小型
**速度：**6格
**视觉：**黑暗视觉

**语言：**通用语，龙语
**技能奖励：**+2地城，+2贼活
**爬虫类：**在考虑有关爬虫类关键字的效果时，你被视为爬虫类。
**陷阱感知：**你在对抗陷阱的攻击的所有防御上获得+2种族加值
**灵活移动：**你具有⟦灵活移动 Shifty Maneuver⟧威能。

⟦灵活移动 Shifty Maneuver⟧

Kobolds overrun dungeons and caverns, relying on vast numbers and wicked traps to make up for their deficiencies in size and strength. Their ability to survive among the bigger and tougher monsters of the world shows just how well their tactics have worked.

Kobolds gather in large tribes, reproducing quickly to replenish their numbers. Group pressure and the dictates of charismatic leaders compel all members in the community to work together toward whatever ends they need to survive. No matter what an individual kobold feels or believes, the community expects obedience, and every kobold in the tribe tries to behave in the expected way. Some kobolds have good hearts, but their chieftains believe only ruthlessness will keep the tribe strong. Thus most kobold tribes commit evil acts, or at least self-serving ones.

Kobolds have few illusions about their place in the world. They are scavengers and thieves. They do not grow their own food and would rather deprive others of their goods than craft anything. They lurk on civilization's fringes, raiding farmsteads and ambushing caravans. They settle in old ruins and dungeons, choosing places they can readily defend and fortify. Even with their great numbers, kobolds know they cannot hope to protect themselves against a determined attacker. For this reason, most tribes raise monstrous allies for added muscle or give in and become servants of dungeon rulers.

Of all the monstrous allies kobolds can make, dragons are best of all. Dragons are everything kobolds are not: enormous, majestic, and powerful. They are gods to the kobolds, their idealized selves, and thus are worthy of worship and service—should any dragon accept the little creatures. Any sign of a dragon sends the tribe into a flurry of activity. The kobolds track it to its lair and present it with sacrifices, pageants, and anything else they think it would like. Of course, a dragon presented with so many willing victims indulges its appetite and gobbles up as many as it can. But death by dragon is no deterrent to the kobolds' efforts. They see being eaten by a god as a great honor, and clamor for their chance to climb into the dragon's maw.

Older dragons see kobolds as nuisances. A quick blast of a breath weapon suffices to eliminate an infestation. The trouble for the dragon is that the kobolds do not give up and might try to serve in secret even if rejected. Younger dragons, however, might see the advantage in a loyal clan of guards and attendants to protect their hoards and warn of adventurers who come calling. Once a kobold tribe installs itself around a dragon, everything they do serves their god.

A kobold's life is unpleasant to say the least. Very few kobolds live to reach old age. Attrition claims most before they get too far into adulthood. Hunger, thirst, and want are constant companions, and even the dimmest kobolds learn to watch their backs. Kobolds are subject to the same greed as dragons, though far less intense. Most of them keep small stashes of coins or other treasure secret from the tribe, even though they know they're duty-bound to pool such resources.

Kobolds understand that they are stronger together than they are apart. All grudges are forgotten when the tribe faces an outside threat. Kobolds demonstrate surprising cunning when dealing with intruders, as evident in the traps they design to level the playing field. Kobolds' skill in trapmaking is amazing. With only minimal supplies—mostly junk— they can fashion crafty snares and clever alarms. Even intrepid explorers know that entering a kobold warren invites disfigurement and death.

The harsh reality of kobold existence demands absolute obedience to the leader's demands. Kobolds who lack the killer's instinct, show any weakness, or disobey orders are shunned and driven to the tribe's periphery. If not devoured by a passing predator or sacrificed to a bloodthirsty god, such exiles might seek their fortunes beyond the tribe. Survival is by no means assured, but such action at least gives them a chance to survive.

Kobolds are survivors first. They are not above prostrating themselves before enemies if it means buying a little time. A lone kobold survivor after a raid, a prisoner, or one otherwise cut off from its fellows must adapt to avoid death. A kobold who was part of an evil tribe might reform its behavior in the presence of others who are willing to guide and support it, and might even find this new "tribe" more comforting than the old one. Such individuals find the adventurer's life suits them—not because they crave danger or excitement, but because their talents make them useful to other adventurers who protect them in return.

---
**外貌特征 Physical Qualities**

Their spare frames and stooped postures don't inspire fear in others, which suits kobolds just fine. They would rather look nonthreatening but not quite vulnerable. A few brave kobolds emulate their honored dragons. They put on a little muscle, raise their snouts high, and roar with a ferocity no one would expect such weak-looking creatures to muster.

Kobolds' long muzzles are lined with tiny teeth and lolling tongues similar to those of a dragon or crocodile. Their slitted eyes are usually red, gold, or yellow. Small horns angle backward from a kobold's brow, and bony barbs stud its forearms to its elbows. Its fingers end in stubby talons, as do its long toes. Fine scales cover a kobold's body, usually some shade of green. Brown, red, and orange scales appear among particular tribes, as do mottled hides of several colors.

Their reptilian anatomy hides kobolds' physical expressiveness from other races. Their facial construction lacks the anatomy to display the same range of emotions as other humanoids. Kobolds who need to deal with warmbloods develop broad arm and head gestures to convey how they feel.

Since kobolds have to make do with what they scavenge, clothing is limited and functional. A loincloth serves the least among them, while warriors cobble together armor from scraps they harvest from the dead. Crude weaponry suffices until they can steal something better.

Kobolds grow quickly. They can walk and talk within hours after hatching and reach their full height after about a year. Kobolds can live longer than a century, though very few make it through their first decade.

**态度和信仰 Attitudes and Beliefs**

Kobolds look after the tribe foremost, and they take whatever steps they deem necessary to ensure the community's survival. The more populous the tribe, the lower the chance any individual will come to harm—even though such large numbers invariably attract attention. Thus, kobolds nurture their eggs in communal nesting grounds to ensure the next generation will preserve their numbers.

Even kobolds who leave their tribes retain the instinct to survive and find comrades. An adventuring kobold regards the party as a small tribe and finds a place to contribute to the group's success. He or she shows an immediate willingness to work within the team, especially if the kobold can tackle a job nobody else in the group is suited for.

Even good-aligned kobolds see little point in fighting with honor. A fair fight achieves nothing if you die. Instead, kobolds admire trickery and subterfuge as virtues and deride as foolish any notion of fairness. The best fight to a kobold is one in which no kobold blood is spilled.

Kobolds see dragons as living gods and offer sacrifices, prayers, and anything else they find to honor their masters. Their devotion stems from their connection to Tiamat, whom they see as their ultimate goddess and mother to all dragons. Kobolds also worship their ancestors, chief among them being Kurtulmak, a figure thought to be one of Tiamat's exarchs. Adventuring kobolds never quite escape their devotion to Tiamat and continue to worship her even if doing so is offensive to their new companions. No kobold wants to face the repercussions of angering such a threatening god.

**狗头人团体 Kobold Communities**

Anyone who examines kobolds' traps can see their ingenuity in construction, yet kobolds do not raise their own towns or strongholds. Instead, they squat in places other peoples have abandoned. A kobold settlement's location must be defensible, offer shelter, and provide enough water and food to support the tribe.

A typical kobold community includes a large common room where the rank and file gather, cook, and sort through the plunder. Nearby is a temple or shrine dedicated to Tiamat, along with chambers set aside for the high priest, the chieftain, and the most accomplished warriors. These rooms offer privacy for the higher-ups without sacrificing the security of having the rest of the tribe nearby.

The passages leading into the warren look safe enough to an outsider, but hidden throughout are all sorts of nasty traps to discourage intruders from venturing too far. Kobolds favor devices that humiliate as much as harm their victims. An adventurer who survives a kobold's trap usually does not do so with pride intact. The tribe might also use rats, scorpions, slimes, or drakes to help guard their warrens.

Kobold tribes not affiliated with dragons freely abandon their lairs if they come under attack. They fight to protect themselves, but should the situation become untenable, they are not above pulling up stakes and settling somewhere else. A dragon's involvement shores up the tribe's courage, and kobolds fight with uncommon boldness to protect their god.

**角色扮演狗头人 Roleplaying a Kobold**

When creating a kobold adventurer, here are a few points to consider.

**You know your way around traps.** Even if another character handles the task of disarming traps, you know enough about their construction to help dismantle them when they are discovered and avoid them when they attack. Traps fascinate you, and any new device is an opportunity to add a weapon to your arsenal. Don't pass up opportunities to tackle a trap and, if possible, try to find ways to turn it to your advantage.

**Fair fights are for suckers.** Concepts such as honor, nobility, and fairness make little sense to you. Death comes soon enough without inviting it through some foolish belief. You use trickery and planning to defeat your enemies. You lure them into danger, drawing them into positions where your allies can finish them off. You hit enemies when they're down, dazed, or otherwise incapacitated. Your survival depends on your willingness to do whatever it takes to win.

**Dragons are gods.** Dragons represent everything kobolds hope to become. Everyone fears them. If dragons are not true gods, they are close enough for you. Encounters with dragons awe you, far beyond the threat they pose. You feel conflicted about fighting dragons and seek a peaceful way out of such an encounter, such as by making an offering or spouting excessive flattery. Should your efforts fail, you still support your allies, but killing the dragon should be the last resort.

**You know your place.** Every kobold in a tribe knows that for the rest to survive, each member must do his or her duty. As an adventuring kobold, you see your companions as your new tribe and search for a way to contribute outside of combat. You might cook meals, mend clothing, or polish armor in addition to fulfilling your role during exploration and combat.

**You exercise caution.** Taking heedless risks can get you killed. Better to be prepared and know what you're getting yourself into. If you get in over your head, fleeing is an important tactic. An enemy that gives chase enters unfamiliar territory, often protected by traps. As a kobold, you feel no shame in running away and expect your companions to do the same should the situation turn against you.

**The world hates you.** Being considered vermin by most people you meet is bound to take a toll. No matter what you accomplish, others might be anything from suspicious to hostile. Even most other reptilian humanoids look down on you, though they're more likely to show you some respect if you prove yourself. When traveling through civilized lands, consider concealing your features to avoid conflicts.

**狗头人特征：**Ambitious, cooperative, fawning, greedy, loyal, obedient, quick, timid

**男性姓名：**Bont, Dartak, Deekin, Forgen, Kol, Meepo, Nin, Speelok, Zeem

**女性姓名：**Capax, Eenith, Foruul, Gumba, Iimen, Lorpe, Rowatak

**部落名字：**Black Death, Broken Fang, Gouger, Red Moon, Skull Kicker, Torn Ear

---
**狗头人辅助威能**

当你的狗头人角色在1级之后获得一个职业辅助威能时，你能选择一个相同或更低等级的狗头人辅助威能来取代该职业辅助威能。

**快撤！ Flee!**

A kobold knows better than to fight against overwhelming odds. Sometimes the only way to win a fight is to escape and fight another day. When it's time to retreat, a kobold leads the way to safety.

**投石索装弹 Load Slingpot**

Kobolds create special sling ammunition made of various substances stored in tiny clay pots. You have learned how to exercise this art through a bit of draconic magic. The magic is unpredictable, however, so you're never sure which enchantment you're going to get.

⟦投石索装弹 Load Slingpot⟧

**隧道疾走 Tunnel Scuttle**

Living in the tight tunnels and unpredictable pathways of a dungeon taught you how to move quickly over precarious terrain. You can climb natural chimneys and fit through tiny spaces, and do it all quickly enough to get away from danger.

⟦隧道疾走 Tunnel Scuttle⟧

**狂乱快步 Frantic Shift**

Cold-blooded kobolds might not look like the quickest creatures, but they can spring about with surprising speed. They prize the ability to move safely and quickly.

⟦狂乱快步 Frantic Shift⟧

**陷阱共享法 Trap-Gang Method**

When kobolds go searching in corridors they believe to be trapped, they work in teams. Working together increases the odds of survival, either because teammates can warn each other or because they can distribute the brunt of a triggered trap's effects. Most big folk don't go in for this sort of thing, so adventuring kobolds "recruit" enemies for the job.

⟦陷阱共享法 Trap-Gang Method⟧

title: 荒野精灵 Wild Elf
body:
属于⟦精灵 Elf⟧的亚种

当你创建一个亚种角色时，你可以自由使用该种族的标准特征，也可以使用亚种提供的选项

每个亚种描述都包含了一些增益。每个增益都会替代一个标准种族特征，正如该增益描述中所提到的。除非另有说明，否则你可以按你所想选择任意数量的亚种的增益

---

在世间所有的妖精生灵中，荒野精灵与大自然的联系最为紧密。事实上，因为唯有他们依然像先祖那样生活，所以许多荒野精灵自视为精类唯一的正统。初看上去，荒野精灵很容易因其身上的涂彩和珠饰被误认为是原始的采集狩猎者。然而，他们的文化中保留着极为繁复深厚的传统，且自皇冠战争时期起便几乎未曾改变。

荒野精灵比日精灵更加奉行孤立主义——甚至往往带有攻击性。偶尔与其他种族打交道的荒野精灵，有时会被族人视为受到了污染。因此，选择与外界建立深厚羁绊的荒野精灵，通常不得不放弃与同族的亲密联系。

**角色扮演荒野精灵 Roleplaying a Wild Elf**

创建荒野精灵角色时，以下几点可供参考。

**外道皆歧途。** 你或许是自愿离开同族，但这并未改变你对世界的看法。在你的同胞眼中，荒野精灵的生活方式之外的一切皆代表着堕落与罪恶。即便你可能比大多数同胞更能接受异族的习俗，也很难彻底放下对他人的戒心。

**天地存万象。** 你将自然世界及其原力视为至亲与益友。你可以从气候的变化、群鸟的飞翔轨迹以及植物的荣枯中读出征兆。而自然秩序无法显现的地方——比如城市、地牢、或是充魔法地形——对你而言都充满危险，因为你无法依靠自己看不懂的征兆。

**因翼而飞，因志而行。** 荒野精灵是必须不断流浪的游牧种族。科瑞隆将这种流浪情结植入了你们的灵魂深处——正是这种冲动，引导着第一批精灵来到这个世界。正如鸟儿羽翼丰满便要高飞一样，每当灵魂受到召唤，你也必须踏上征途。

**荒野精灵增益 Wild Elf Benefits**

当创造荒野精灵角色时，你可以从下列增益中挑选。

**狡黠步：**荒野精灵从能走路起就开始接受战斗训练，他们的导师很早就强调闪避与逃脱。待荒野精灵成长为战士时，这些儿时所学的技能既能使他们深入战斗，也能从容脱身。

增益：每遭遇一次，你能以一个移动动作快步最多等同于你的速度的格数。此增益替代「精灵之精准」

**荒野精灵武器擅长：**虽然雅灵专注于长剑，但荒野精灵数千年来一直依赖传统狩猎武器——矛。

增益：你获得标枪、矛和长矛的擅长。此增益替代「团体警觉」

title: 机关人 Warforged
body:
**为了已终结的战争而被创造，找寻着生存的意义所在。**

**平均身高：**183cm-198cm/6'0"–6'6"
**平均体重：**122kg-136kg/270-300 lb

**属性调整：**+2体质；+2力量或智力
**体型：**中型
**速度：**6格
**视觉：**普通视觉

**语言：**通用语
**技能奖励：**+2坚韧，+2威吓
**活体构装：**你是一个活体构装体。你不需要进食，饮水，呼吸，和睡眠。你不需要进行坚韧检定来对抗饥饿，干渴和窒息。其他状态依然正常对你造成影响。
**无眠哨兵：**你不需要睡眠，而只是进入一种持续4小时的静止状态以获得长休息的好处。在这个状态下，你可以充分注意到周围的情况，并且可以如常发现敌人接近或者其他事件。
**机关人韧性：**你在对抗持续伤害的豁免骰上获得+2种族加值。同时，当你进行死亡豁免检定时，你可以使用你掷出的更好的结果或取10。
**机关人意志：**你在意志上获得+1种族加值。
**机关人决心：**你具有⟦机关人决心 Warforged Resolve⟧威能。

⟦机关人决心 Warforged Resolve⟧

身为天生的士兵，机关人是拥有人类的智慧以及自我意识的人造物，象征着一个时代的终结。但机关人所发展出的知觉，却是由于他们创造者希望创造出一种能自行适应战场的完美战争机器所产生的副作用。当没有大规模战争的可以参与，也没有远古的遗物需要争夺，只剩下一些不到百年的文明遗迹时，机关人就成为了一支新独立的族群。在融入了由那些人数远比它们更多的种族所建立的社会之后，机关人以其坚韧和专注而闻名，工作起来和战斗同样出色。

扮演一名机关人，如果你希望…

• 强壮、结实、为战斗而生的角色。
• 搜寻你存在的意义
• 成为偏爱战士，野蛮人，守望者和圣武士的种族的一员

---
**外貌特征 Physical Qualities**

机关人是由钢铁及石头构成的笨重类人生物。在由类似材料制成的骨架，以及由皮革和木质纤维束制成的肌肉系统的支撑下，机关人体内有一套充满了血样液体的内置管路系统，维护和润滑着其它系统。他们有力的手臂末端是只有两根手指和一根拇指的的手，他们的脚上也只有两根宽大的脚趾。

机关人的头部拥有简单的人类特征，拥有阴沉的表情以及由铰链连接且没有牙齿的下顎。他们也没有鼻子。当经历剧烈的感情时，他们的眼睛有时会发光，同时他们的前额和头顶浮现出符纹的线条。每一个机关人的前额都有一个独特的符文，就像人类拥有独特的指纹一般。这个符文读作“Ghulra”，是在魔神语中表示“真理”的文字。

机关人拥有明显是人造而且无性别差异的外观。他们不能像其他的类人生物般繁殖自身。然而，它们的痛觉似乎仅限于受伤，这让它们可以很容易的改装自己的身体。这类身体改装也让机关人像其他种族般，拥有著各式各样的外表。

**角色扮演机关人 Roleplaying a Warforged**

Warforged have a straightforward emotional range. Although they experience pain, fear, hatred, and anger like other races, they are reserved and pensive, hiding emotions behind expressionless metal faces. Some warforged lack introspection and are dangerously naïve or emotionally stunted. Many warforged are the opposite, though. They question the purpose of their existence and consider whether or not they have souls. A few warforged develop sophisticated philosophies about what they perceive and learn. Many warforged fall in with humanoids of similar mindsets, working passionately for an organization or a religion. A warforged typically forms a strong emotional attachment to a small group of comrades.

A warforged often has limited experiences in the world, having spent its existence assigned to one specific duty. Warforged enjoy working, and many create endless lists of goals and chores. They take pride in their jobs, and they dislike idleness and failure more than most races do. A warforged's sensibilities give it a single-minded efficiency with any task, particularly in combat. War and military conditioning color warforged behavior. Warforged intuitively understand duty, conflict, the chain of command, and other elements of war and soldierly life.

Because most warforged have bodies that resemble males, they identify themselves as males and prefer to be called “he” rather than “it.” Some warforged adopt female names, though. Most warforged have simple names related to their jobs, abilities, or military positions. Warforged often accept the names or the nicknames that their comrades give them, although some search long for particular names that define them. Many simply take names common within another race, especially those of humans.

**机关人特征：**好斗的、机警的、无畏的、好奇的、直率的、勤奋的、忠诚的、守序的、天真的、老练的、沉默的、纯朴的。

**机关人姓名：**Azm, Book, Bulwark, Cutter, Falchion, Graven, Hammer, Mark, Morg, Nameless, Pierce, Pious, Relic, Rune, Steeple, Three, Titan, Unsung, Victor, Watcher, Zealot

**吉斯洋基的意志力：**你在意志上获得+1加值，且你在对抗魅惑效果的豁免检定上获得+2加值。
**意念转移：**你具有⟦意念转移 Telekinetic Leap⟧威能。

⟦意念转移 Telekinetic Leap⟧

作为奴隶出身的种族，吉斯洋基人是凶悍的心灵战士，他们定期在众星之海中往来，使用银剑作战。

吉斯洋基人和吉斯泽雷人曾经同是一个被灵吸怪奴役的种族——吉斯人，但是在他们争取来自由之后，他们分裂成了两个种族。吉斯泽雷人逃到元素混沌，逐渐成为了自省的修行者，而吉斯洋基人逃到了众星之海，逐渐成为了仇外的军国主义者。吉斯洋基人建立了根据地和军队，然后启程去征服挡在他们道路上的一切。

---

很久很久以前，原始的吉斯人从他们的灵吸怪统治者手下逃脱，然而却在激烈的内战下分化出吉斯洋基人和吉斯泽雷人这两个对手。随着时间流逝，吉斯洋基人建立了一种暴政，这种暴政制度的残忍嗜血程度几乎和曾经奴役他们的灵吸怪们一样。吉斯洋基人只要一见到灵吸怪就会发动攻击，另外，他们对待他们的亲戚吉斯泽雷人的态度也是一样。

吉斯洋基人说通用语。他们也从灵吸怪统治者那学会了异怪语

吉斯洋基人的城市和根据地都建立在众星之海中无名和荒废的死物上。吉斯洋基人在众星之海里使用星界飞船航行，寻找已死去的神祗和已毁坏的领域的残片来增强他们自己的要塞，丰富他们自己的储藏。偶尔，他们会把视线放到其他世界，下定决心去进行洗劫一空。

吉斯洋基人没有家庭，他们一出生就属于一些被称为“骨干”的军事训练机构。一个吉斯洋基人会异乎寻常地重视自己的“骨干”，另外一个特点是，他们从不会知道自己父母和兄弟姐妹的名字。对一个吉斯洋基人来说，比“骨干”更重要的是他自己的武器。吉斯洋基人甚至会重视自己的武器多过于重视自己的同伴。

图纳拉斯是最大的吉斯洋基城市，它建立在一个漂浮在众星之海的死亡神祗身上，被Vlaakith这位吉斯洋基人的巫妖女王所统治着，她已经统治了超过1000年了。吉斯洋基人把这位巫妖女王当作他们种族的母亲一样尊敬着。对他们来说，她的话就是真理。据说，她会把任何挑战她的政策和权威的人除掉，吞噬掉他们的生命元素。

吉斯洋基人和红龙有着契约，这在某些时候允许吉斯洋基人骑乘红龙。

title: 吉斯泽雷人 Githzerai
body:
**苦行与戒律，为身心之主宰。**

**平均身高：**183cm-196cm/6'-6'5"
**平均体重：**73kg-86kg/160-190 lb
